newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says does not see excessive wage claims.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says does not see excessive wage claims.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) deputy governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday he did not expect unions to push for excessive wage increases.
Macfarlane is to take over as governor of the central bank later this month.
Macfarlane said the bank and the government aimed to keep underlying inflation between two and three percent over the course of the economic cycle.

"In an environment where ... the central bank and the govenment have that aim, it would be extremely unfortunate if wage settlements, if the trade union movement were to aim for an average increase in wage settlements which was not consistent with that," Macfarlane said.
"I think in some particular industries it's happening, but I think on average we don't think that they will."
Australia's Liberal-National government has forecast average earnings to increase 5.0 percent in the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, from 4.0 percent in 1995/96.
The Treasury said in the 1996/97 budget that wages pressures were not expected to intensify over the year, but that they needed continued policy vigilance.
The Reserve Bank has previously expressed concern that the level of annual wage increases should not exceed 4.5 percent to avoid threatening low inflation.
